doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Early influences Urbie Green, Watrous and discovering Carl Fontana
summary: He explains hunting down Carl Fontana's records and learning his time feel and phrasing without copying notes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. Seemingly completely effortless when he plays. And it really knocked me out. And so I was really getting into him and Urbie. And someone said, “well you know Bill Watrous’s influence is is Carl Fontana.” So I said, “oh, who’s Carl Fontana?” And at the time Carl had no albums out under his own name. He didn’t record any albums under his own name until like 1986 or something like that. So I had to hunt for him. The first album I found was “SuperSax,” that SuperSax album that he’s featured on four or five tunes. Then he did a co-led album “Live at the Concord Jazz Festival,” Hanna-Fontana Band with Jake Hanna. So technically I guess he led that group. But I wore those albums out. Because I realized okay Bill was on some here. This is the source. And the one thing I knew early on was I didn’t want to sound exactly like anybody. So I thought okay, let’s do what Bill did. We’ll go back and listen to Carl and we’ll see how that affects what I do through what I’ve been studying with Urbie, and obviously I discovered J.J. by that time, and Curtis Fuller and all these people. And Carl’s — the first thing that struck me was the way he played time. His eighth note feel, how relaxed everything was, that really took to me immediately. And that’s really what I wanted to go for there. So I kind of put him up on a pedestal for quite a long time, really trying to get close to his way of phrasing. Not the way he played notes, I mean I played similar things that he played, but I wasn’t about like transcribing everything he did and playing it note for note. I wanted to just kind of get a sense for what his approach was and as far as inflections and time feel and all that stuff.
